html:
Samudera Pasai was a Muslim kingdom on the north coast of Sumatra from the late 1200s to the early 1500s, the first known Muslim dynasty in the Indonesian archipelago.

Tradition says it was founded by a local ruler, Merah Silu, who converted to Islam and took the name Malik al Saleh. His gravestone, dated 1297, is one of the earliest Muslim royal tombs in the region. The port sat at the north end of the Strait of Malacca, where ships from India and Arabia arrived, and it grew rich on pepper, gold and trade. Muslim merchants from Gujarat and elsewhere brought the faith.

The traveller Ibn Battuta stopped there in 1345 and 1346 on his way to China and described a Muslim sultan who loved debating religious law. Pasai minted gold coins and its scholars spread Islam to other ports. It was raided by Majapahit and later overshadowed by the Malacca Sultanate. The Portuguese took it in 1521, and it was absorbed by Aceh in 1524.
sum: Samudera Pasai was a Muslim kingdom on the north coast of Sumatra from the late 1200s to the early 1500s, the first known Muslim dynasty in the Indonesian archipelago.
